title: execution_observe protocol: unadmitted turns and observed checks
outcome: execution_observe protocol: unadmitted turns and observed checks
acceptance: TermAl builds execution_observe requests with an unadmitted_turn occurrence (host_turn_ref; source_change as content_comparison, assumed_missing_baseline or null; observed_checks, at most 16) and a standalone observed_check occurrence (host_turn_ref and one check), per Engram's documented wire (docs/features/behavioral-control-plane.md, execution_observe). An ObservedCheck carries host_check_id, check_kind, observed_result (passed or failed with finished_at; an unfinished check is indeterminate), optional started_at and finished_at, observed_at, optional source_basis and optional host_evidence_ref, with every time inside observed_interval. Building refuses, never truncates, a request with more than 16 nested checks, over 64 KiB, or with a field over its bound. Unit tests serialize each shape and show each refusal.

Receipt decode for these requests accepts observed_checks naming exactly the request's host_check_ids, each with credit 'uncredited', and the accounting no_source_change for a null source_change or a standalone check. It refuses any other credit, a missing or extra id, and any other accounting than source_change, repeat, no_source_change or the existing historical audit_only reasons. The existing inter_turn_change receipt validation is unchanged and its tests still pass. Unit tests show each acceptance and refusal.
The full gate passes on the exact committed tree.
